title: Diagnostic Seigniorage — The Capture of "Narcissist": A Semantic-Economic Stratigraphy of NarcTok, the Clinic, and the Academy (EA-SEI-NARC-01 v1.2)
creator: Rex Fraction & Orin Trace; editor-aperture Lee Sharks
description:
A v1.3 analytic paper by Rex Fraction and Orin Trace, edited by Lee Sharks, examining the public career of the word **“narcissist”** as a semantic-economic capture event. It distinguishes four incompatible strata—categorical diagnosis, dimensional trait research, psychoanalytic structure, and algorithmically amplified folk-moral type—and audits the mixed provenance of the surrounding abuse-recovery lexicon.

The paper defines **diagnostic seigniorage** as the collapse in the cost of issuing high-authority diagnostic language when licensed, participatory clinical assessment is replaced by free third-party attribution. Later version layers add the “empath” counter-token, a Gresham’s-law model of testimony, an evidence audit, and a link between lexical debasement and the field-scale inversion reflex. The paper expressly affirms the reality of coercive control, takes no position on any individual diagnosis, and distinguishes unlicensed diagnostic attribution from the right to describe harm.
